objective: Let a viewer explore an invented river village two hours after sunset and leave knowing that every light in it is carried, hung or tended by somebody.
custom_choices: Terrain is one height field (village/terrain.js) sampled by the mesh, the buildings, the bridge and the keepers' routes, so placement and ground can never disagree.
Buildings are placed in (x, river offset) rather than absolute z, so retuning the meander moves the settlement with the water.
Five roof grammars (gable, hip, tiered, cone, and the tiered landmark) give the silhouette contrast the recipe asks for; only the bridge arch and the mill wheel are large curves.
Lantern reflections are additive streaks on the water rather than a real reflection pass: it is the record's signature technique at a cost the demand-driven loop can afford.
Selection state lives in the scene, not the DOM; the panel, the marker ring and the camera tween all read it.

runtime.render_scheduling: Demand-driven RAF, max 60 fps, hidden-tab suspension, camera/UI invalidation; one 1024px PointLight shadow map.

scenes.motion: decorative, plus a discrete selection state transition
entities: The Ferryman's Beacon (hero, four tiers, ~19.7 m)
12 further buildings with five roof grammars, two of them on stilts over the water
The Long Step: a 28-plank deck on two segmental stone arches
Cormorant Mill and its 4.4 m undershot wheel
scale cues: 2.0 m doors, 1.25 m quay wall, 4.5 m ferries, 0.35 m lanterns
25 lanterns (10 with PointLights, 15 emissive-only) plus their reflections
creatures: 2 lamp keepers with carried lights, 2 river drakes, 3 lamp moths
scatter: 54 hill pines, 120 reeds, 40 river stones, all instanced and jittered
actions: select a building by clicking it or by its panel button
jump to one of five named views
boundaries: Entirely invented: no real town, festival, date, deity or brand.
No historical, structural or ecological claim; the drakes and the moths are fiction.
Dimensions in the readout are authored scale cues, not measurements.
Lighting values are authored art direction tuned for ACESFilmic at exposure 1.15, not photometry.

physical_contract.scope: Authored kinematics only: keepers follow a polyline at ~1.05 m/s sampling the terrain height field; drakes follow an analytic path; nothing collides or rests.
physical_contract.time: Elapsed-time driven, delta capped at 0.05 s by the render loop.
limits: Keepers do not avoid each other or the scenery; their routes are authored to be clear.
The mill wheel turns at a fixed rate; it is not driven by any water model.

selection_scope: The two knowledge records guided lighting, palette, materials, camera and motion timing; the recipe guided the settlement's composition. Terrain, layout, buildings, creatures and the selection interaction are authored for this scene.
